node-autoscaling.questions.0.prompt: Adding Pods did not help because all nodes are full. How would you divide the investigation between workload scaling and node provisioning?
node-autoscaling.questions.0.points.0: Separate HPA replica decisions from scheduler placement and node capacity.
node-autoscaling.questions.0.points.1: Check unschedulable requests, placement constraints and the provisioner’s allowed node shapes.
node-autoscaling.questions.0.points.2: Node startup, quotas and disruption budgets affect recovery time; no cloud action is performed in this lab.
node-autoscaling.questions.1.prompt: Why could a Karpenter consolidation plan reduce cost but still be unsafe for a stateful workload?
node-autoscaling.questions.1.points.0: Check application replication, disruption budgets and volume topology before replacing capacity.
node-autoscaling.questions.1.points.1: Respect startup and draining time; cheaper capacity alone does not prove availability.
node-autoscaling.questions.1.points.2: A NodePool describes allowed capacity; it does not replace application recovery design.
node-autoscaling.title: Cluster Autoscaler and Karpenter
traffic-strategies.questions.0.prompt: A team wants a small live canary and a traffic mirror. Which observations and side effects differ between those experiments?
traffic-strategies.questions.0.points.0: A canary serves a chosen share of real users; compare errors, latency and business signals.
traffic-strategies.questions.0.points.1: A mirror duplicates requests while its responses are normally not returned to users.
traffic-strategies.questions.0.points.2: Duplicated writes, credentials and personal data require explicit safeguards; no Istio or external traffic runs here.
traffic-strategies.questions.1.prompt: What is missing if a plain Service selects nine stable replicas and one candidate and the team calls this a guaranteed ten-percent canary?
traffic-strategies.questions.1.points.0: Endpoint counts approximate distribution but do not guarantee per-request percentages or user stickiness.
traffic-strategies.questions.1.points.1: Connection reuse, readiness and client behavior change observed traffic share.
traffic-strategies.questions.1.points.2: Use measured traffic and a routing implementation when a precise split or cohort rule is required.
traffic-strategies.title: Canary and shadow deployments
recovery-design.questions.0.prompt: The control-plane snapshot restored successfully, but a database volume is empty. Which recovery assumptions failed?
recovery-design.questions.0.points.0: etcd holds Kubernetes API state; it does not contain the application data stored on every persistent volume.
recovery-design.questions.0.points.1: Recover the application data and external dependencies with a consistent backup method.
recovery-design.questions.0.points.2: A restore rehearsal must verify usable application state, not only healthy cluster components.
recovery-design.questions.1.prompt: How would you turn a target of fifteen minutes of data loss and one hour of downtime into a testable recovery plan?
recovery-design.questions.1.points.0: Treat the loss target as RPO and the downtime target as RTO.
recovery-design.questions.1.points.1: Measure backup frequency, copy delay, restore duration and dependency recovery.
recovery-design.questions.1.points.2: Run an isolated restore and check data timestamps and application behavior against both targets.
recovery-design.title: Developing disaster recovery plans
architecture-runtime.title: Runtime and control-plane boundaries
architecture-runtime.questions.0.prompt: A container works locally but its Pod remains Pending. Which boundaries would you investigate before rebuilding the image?
The API accepts desired state; scheduling chooses a feasible node, while kubelet and the CRI runtime start containers.
Inspect scheduling events, requests and placement constraints before attributing Pending to application code.
architecture-runtime.questions.1.prompt: When would a VM provide an isolation property that an ordinary container does not?
Ordinary containers share the host kernel; namespaces and cgroups do not create a separate guest kernel.
A VM adds a guest-kernel boundary and costs more resources; choose according to trust and workload constraints.
vertical-scaling.title: Vertical scaling decisions
vertical-scaling.questions.0.prompt: An HPA adds replicas but every replica is OOMKilled. What would you measure before adding a VPA?
vertical-scaling.questions.0.points.0: Inspect working-set growth, limits, OOM evidence and whether memory is per-process or shared external state.
vertical-scaling.questions.0.points.1: A VPA recommendation is evidence for right-sizing, not proof that a leak has been fixed.
vertical-scaling.questions.0.points.2: This single-node lab does not run VPA or resize nodes.
vertical-scaling.questions.1.prompt: Why can simultaneous HPA and VPA changes create a feedback loop?
vertical-scaling.questions.1.points.0: CPU utilization targets depend on requests; changing requests changes the utilization denominator.
vertical-scaling.questions.1.points.1: Separate control signals or constrain policies; test disruption and capacity before automatic updates.
platform-boundaries.title: Storage, networking and security boundaries
platform-boundaries.questions.0.prompt: A PVC is Bound, but its application cannot recover on another node. Which storage assumptions need evidence?
platform-boundaries.questions.0.points.0: Binding alone does not prove portable data, cross-zone access or replication; inspect the driver, access modes and topology.
platform-boundaries.questions.0.points.1: The lab verifies local claims and retained data; multi-node CSI failure and off-host backup remain design questions.
platform-boundaries.questions.1.prompt: A namespace passes Restricted admission and NetworkPolicy checks. What cluster protections are still unproven?
platform-boundaries.questions.1.points.0: Admission and L3/L4 filtering do not prove kernel isolation, encrypted traffic, safe node credentials or protected etcd backups.
platform-boundaries.questions.1.points.1: Evaluate CNI behavior, TLS identities, node hardening and secret access separately; no host or global policy is changed here.
availability-design.title: Availability and failure domains
availability-design.questions.0.prompt: Three replicas run on one node. Which failures can they tolerate, and which remain shared?
availability-design.questions.0.points.0: Replica replacement can cover a process or Pod failure while the node is healthy.
availability-design.questions.0.points.1: Node, storage, network and power failures remain shared; anti-affinity needs actual independent capacity.
availability-design.questions.1.prompt: Why does a highly available control plane not guarantee that a user request succeeds?
availability-design.questions.1.points.0: The data path also depends on routing, ready workloads, data and external services.
availability-design.questions.1.points.1: Define user-visible signals and failure domains; test recovery beyond API availability.
availability-design.questions.1.points.2: Control-plane quorum and multi-zone recovery are discussed, not simulated by one kind node.
observability-signals.title: Choosing diagnostic signals
observability-signals.questions.0.prompt: Prometheus reports up=1, yet users see slow responses. Which additional evidence would you seek?
observability-signals.questions.0.points: up proves the scrape succeeded, not application correctness or user latency.
Measure request latency, errors and saturation; use correlated logs or traces to locate the slow dependency.
observability-signals.questions.1.prompt: Why should request IDs usually stay out of a Prometheus label?
observability-signals.questions.1.points: An unbounded label value creates many time series and increases ingestion, memory and query costs.
Use bounded metric dimensions and put per-request detail in logs or traces with controlled retention.
interview-reasoning.title: Explaining an investigation
interview-reasoning.questions.0.prompt: An interviewer asks for the cause of an outage after showing only a restart count. How do you answer without guessing?
interview-reasoning.questions.0.points.0: State what is observed and which causes remain hypotheses; request termination state, events and relevant logs.
interview-reasoning.questions.0.points.1: Choose one discriminating check, describe its possible results and revise the hypothesis from evidence.
interview-reasoning.questions.1.prompt: How do you explain a successful repair without presenting the lab as production experience?
interview-reasoning.questions.1.points.0: Name the lab context, your actual action and the measured before/after behavior.
interview-reasoning.questions.1.points.1: Separate verified mechanisms from untested scale, high availability and business impact.
